look_here_first: FIND THE ROSETTE and a WHOLE LEAF. Cedar sage is a taprooted PERENNIAL with low rosette and stem leaves, usually on long petioles; leaves can be simple (one terminal leaflet) or pinnately 3-foliolate with two smaller lateral leaflets. Many basal blades rounded/heart-shaped, unlike scarlet sage's simple deltoid leaves up an upright stem or big red sage's broad, thick, smooth rosette. Then inspect red tubular flowers and shaded cedar-juniper habitat.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: very long petioles; some leaves can appear nearly peltate in field view

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey highlights the red tubular flower and the unusually long petioles, describing the leaves as nearly peltate in appearance. This is a useful field cue when the basal rosette is visible.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Taprooted rosetted woodland perennial, one to several ascending flower stems from basal crown; often under Ashe juniper in leafy duff/limestone shade.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: UT Austin: opposite, 1–3 foliolate, often seemingly a single broad terminal leaflet with cordate base or two smaller lateral leaflets; long petioles, terminal blade to about 50 × 55 mm, soft/velveteen hair. Some leaves appear nearly peltate but petiole actually attaches at leaf base.

key_traits.label: Flowering nodes
key_traits.text: Paired three-flowered cymes at successive flowering nodes; red/crimson tubular corollas and persistent calyx, calyx green with purple ridges/tips.

key_traits.label: Flower measurement
key_traits.text: UT Austin corolla tube/throat to about 17 mm plus lips ~11.5 mm (complex overlapping measures); do NOT present as a 4-cm Big Red sage flower.

key_traits.label: Diagnostic calyx
key_traits.text: Calyx roughly 11 mm tube length, purplish veined and long-pointed at upper tip; measure with scale if teaching fine IDs.

key_traits.label: Habit vs big red
key_traits.text: Both rosetted, but Big Red sage's thick, dark-green smooth basal leaves to 12 cm and pink-red 4 cm corollas on 1.5 m stalks are usually much larger and often moist ravine/seep-associated.
